title: Even Squares and Odd Count
statement: You are given n integers. Print two lines. On line 1, print the sum of the squares of all even numbers. On line 2, print how many numbers are odd. Zero is even. Negative numbers count too: -3 is odd and -4 is even. If there is no even number, the sum is 0. Use streams in your solution.
inputFormat: Line 1: the integer n. Line 2: n integers separated by single spaces.
outputFormat: Line 1: the sum of squares of the even numbers. Line 2: the count of odd numbers.
constraints: The sum can be larger than the int limit, so use long
explanations: The even numbers are 2 and 4. Their squares are 4 and 16, and the sum is 20. The odd numbers are 1, 3 and 5, so the count is 3.
The even numbers are -2, 0 and 10. Their squares are 4, 0 and 100, and the sum is 104. Only 7 is odd, so the count is 1.
reference:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0])
v = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
print(sum(x * x for x in v if x % 2 == 0))
print(sum(1 for x in v if x % 2 != 0))
